full_judgment: 8. The defendant has contested in the revisional application by filing Vokalatnama but did not file any counter-affidavit. Mr Bivash Chandra Biswas, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party No. 1 has submitted that the Rule is not maintainable, he has contended that parties are the predecessor, of the original owner that is Huzzatullah and, as such, the plaintiff ought to have filed the suit for declaration along with a prayer for partition. Learned Advocate has supported the judgment of the appellate Court and further submitted that the appellate Court has considered the facts and circumstances of the case and has rightly allowed the appeal. He has further submitted that the Kabuliyat of 1922 has not been properly proved by the plaintiff but the trial Court without considering the same has passed the judgment and decree which has rightly been set aside by the appellate Court. He has further contended that the land of the plaintiff has not been identified in the suit, as such, the trial Court has not passed the judgment in a proper manner, the appellate Court being the last Court of fact has taken all the aspects into consideration and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court in a lawful manner.
